source: Ministry of Agriculture training module "ជំនិតកម្មដំណាំខ្នុរសំរាប់កសិកម្ម" (Jackfruit Cultivation Techniques for Agriculture), prepared with participation from the Santisena organization, an elderly people's association, a charitable organization, and the CRS (Catholic Relief Services) agriculture program; content compiled with reference to fruit-tree materials and Prek Leap National School of Agriculture (សាលាជាតិកសិកម្មព្រែកលៀប).
text:
Seeds selected for sowing should be buried two to three days after the fruit's flesh is eaten out. Spread the seeds on the already-prepared nursery bed, spacing them a short, consistent distance apart, seed to seed. Cover the seeds with soil, pressing the soil down firmly and evenly over them. Cover the bed with a thin layer of chopped straw mulch, and water it regularly to keep it moist.

The illustration shows the seeds laid out in rows on the bed and a worker placing seeds by hand at a small, regular spacing. Note: the exact spacing figures shown in the diagram's small numeric labels were not fully legible in the scan, so precise spacing values are not given here rather than guessed.
